home.amuni_text: Amunì is not just an invitation to travel, it is the embrace of our land. It means 'let's do it together': do not watch from afar, but enter the pulse of the village. When we say Amunì, we are erasing the border between those who arrive and those who stay, to make every step a shared discovery.

castle.title: Caccamo Castle
castle.rhyme_1:
Welcome, wanderers, to the mighty manor,
gazing at the valley and history's splendor.
Perched on the mountain of proud living stone,
guardian of dreams, glory, and the unknown.
castle.rhyme_2:
Within these walls that defy the flow of time,
dynasties passed like a breeze in their prime.
From the proud Chiaramonte, adventurous and bold,
every room tells of pacts and stories of old.
castle.rhyme_3:
Do not seek dates in a cold, dusty tome,
but the shadow that dances as evening has come.
The Castellana awaits, with secrets to share,
of Sister Felicia, and the paths everywhere.
castle.welcomemsg_felicia: Welcome to Caccamo Castle, stranger. I am Sister Felicia. Would you like me to reveal the secrets of the Conspiracy Room, or do you prefer to hear the ancient legends of the manor? Just ask.
castle.position: A fortress perched on a rocky spur, with a dominant view over the valley.
castle.defense: Loopholes, thick walls, and patrol walkways recount its defensive function.
castle.conspiracy: Secret rooms and noble chambers were the stage for medieval conspiracies and intrigues.
castle.prisons: The underground prisons still guard the traces of ancient detentions.
castle.legend_brothers: The legend of the two brothers tells of a fatal duel for a lady's love.

castello.title: Caccamo Castle
castello.description: Caccamo Castle is among the largest and best-preserved Norman fortresses in Sicily. Perched on living rock since the 11th century, it dominates the San Leonardo valley with its imposing walls, watchtowers, and evocative interior halls that recall centuries of feudal history and chivalric legends.
castello.hours: Every day: 09:30 AM – 01:00 PM / 03:00 PM – 07:00 PM

badia.title: Church of San Benedetto alla Badia
badia.description: A true jewel of Sicilian Baroque, the church is famous worldwide for its extraordinary floor made entirely of 18th-century majolica, depicting allegorical scenes and naturalistic motifs of rare mastery. A masterpiece of visual art suspended in time.
badia.hours: Tue - Sun: 09:00 AM – 12:30 PM | Mon: 02:30 PM – 06:30 PM (No regular services, ideal for visits)
badia.tickets: Full € 2.00 | Reduced € 1.00 (EU youth 18-25 or with Castle ticket same day) | Under 18 Free

santamaria.title: Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli
santamaria.description: Founded in the 15th century along with the Dominican convent, the Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli is one of the most important spiritual centers of the village. It houses the remains and relics of Blessed Giovanni Liccio, Patron of Caccamo. Inside, you can admire splendid marble altars and works of sacred art that bear witness to centuries of deep devotion and pilgrimages.
santamaria.hours: Open for visits: Saturday 4:00 PM – 5:30 PM | Sunday 9:00 AM – 10:00 AM and 11:00 AM – 12:30 PM. (Holy Masses: Saturday 5:30 PM | Sunday 10:00 AM).

sangiorgio.title: Church of San Giorgio Martire
sangiorgio.description: The Mother Church of Caccamo, dedicated to Saint George the Martyr, is an imposing masterpiece dominating the monumental square below the Castle. Founded in the Norman era and rebuilt in 1614, it preserves an immense artistic heritage: from Gagini-school sculptures to precious 17th-century paintings by Flemish artist Matthias Stom, to rich chapels decorated in mixed marbles.
sangiorgio.hours: Visiting hours: Saturday and Sunday 9:30 AM – 10:45 AM and 4:00 PM – 6:00 PM. (Tourist reception is suspended during Sunday Mass at 11:00 AM).

annunziata.title: Parish of the Most Holy Annunziata
annunziata.description: Nestled in the medieval urban fabric, the church stands out for its facade and the atmosphere of deep spirituality found inside. It preserves finely decorated altars and artistic artifacts that attract visitors and the faithful.
annunziata.hours: Mon - Sat: 09:00 AM – 12:00 PM | Weekday Masses 6:00 PM. Sundays and Holidays: 08:30 AM - 09:30 AM and 10:30 AM - 12:00 PM (Holiday Masses 9:30 AM, 12:00 PM, 7:00 PM).

cappuccini.title: Capuchin Friars Convent
cappuccini.description: A place of silence, meditation, and history, the Convent structures are deeply linked to the Franciscan tradition in Sicily. In addition to the convent structure, the area offers an authentic insight into monastic life and popular devotion.
cappuccini.hours: Accessible mainly upon request or during Franciscan holidays. Contact the Tourism Office.
cappuccini.secret_info: 💡 The Hidden Jewels of Caccamo: The village is home to 33 churches. Use the Din Don Dan map and zoom in on Caccamo to discover the hours and real-time openings of lesser-known treasures like the Church of San Rocco and other small scattered masterpieces.

chiese_page.poesia_intro:
Five temples of stone, of faith and of memory,
open their doors to a centurial story.
chiese_page.verse_angeli:
At the Angels rests, in the most sacred silence,
Blessed Giovanni, the village's presence.
chiese_page.verse_badia:
If you descend to the Badia, the earth turns to flower,
in the majolica embroidery of rare power.
chiese_page.verse_duomo:
Enter the great Duomo, majestic and grand,
amidst Gagini's marbles and Stomer's hand.
chiese_page.verse_annunziata:
Then the Annunziata reveals painted vaults so bright,
and the bell tower that guards through the night.
chiese_page.verse_cappuccini:
Finally climb to the Capuchins, on the hill so fair,
between an altarpiece and a panorama rare.
chiese_page.poesia_outro: Let yourself be guided where time has stood still...

transport_page.welcome: Welcome, traveler, to the Transport section. Here you will find the necessary information to move around the surroundings of the village.
transport_page.company_desc: The bus lines connect Caccamo to Termini Imerese and Palermo all year round. Taking the afternoon route to Palermo, you can get off at Vetrana, a renowned seaside area. From Termini Imerese, you can also take the train to Cefalù and other tourist destinations.
transport_page.stop_1: Porta Euracea: in front of Bar Giallombardo and the building materials store.
transport_page.stop_2: Viale Regione Siciliana: above the 'Roberta' playground (near the Axa insurance agency).
transport_page.stop_3: Piazza Cappuccini: in the shade of the ancient Convent.

events_page.title: Rites and Festivals of the Borough
events_page.intro: Experience the most authentic soul of our village through its centuries-old traditions, where faith, history, and folklore intertwine in unique and emotional moments.
events_page.signuruzzu_desc: On Palm Sunday, a local child impersonates Jesus and parades on a donkey decorated with palms through the streets of the village decked out for the party. The procession stops in front of the Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli and the Duomo of San Giorgio Martire for the evocative blessing.
events_page.venerdi_desc: The atmosphere becomes profound with the altars set up in the churches for Good Friday, enriched with the typical plates of wheat germinated in the dark. This is followed by the solemn and moving Procession and the town's Via Crucis.
events_page.giovanni_desc: A deeply felt and experienced recurrence by the entire community, which gathers around its Blessed in a climate of great devotion and popular warmth.
events_page.castellana_title: Election of the Castellana & Historical Parade
events_page.castellana_desc: The village dives back into its glorious medieval past. A majestic historical parade in period costumes crosses the streets, culminating in the solemn election of the Castellana of the manor.
events_page.nicasio_title: Feast of Saint Nicasio and the Palio
events_page.nicasio_desc: Vibrant celebrations in honor of the Saint, enriched by the highly anticipated and gripping city Palio that ignites the challenge and enthusiasm of young and old.
events_page.sagra_desc: Every year, on October 12th, the scents of tradition invade the village. An unmissable gastronomic appointment to taste the authentic local sausage amidst songs, wine, and conviviality.
